item.title: Every Song That Topped the UK Chart for 8 or More Weeks, But Didn’t Make the Top 10 on the Hot 100
item.description:
[Energetic music fades out, and the host speaks]
Host: "Welcome to the latest update on the world of music charts. I've got some interesting facts to share with you today. Let's start with the current No. 1 single in the U.K. - 'Rein Me In' by Sam Fender and Olivia Dean. For the 10th non-consecutive week, it's holding strong at the top of the Official Singles Chart.
[Short music transition]
Host: "But here's the thing - despite its massive success in the U.K., 'Rein Me In' hasn't quite broken through in the same way in the U.S. It's currently sitting at No. 80 on the Billboard Hot 100, after previously reaching as high as No. 64. This makes it one of only three singles to log 10 or more weeks at No. 1 in the U.K. without reaching the top 10 on the Hot 100.
[Short music transition]
Host: "Now, you might be wondering - what other songs have achieved this feat? Well, 'Rein Me In' joins an exclusive club with Wet Wet Wet's 'Love Is All Around' and Dave & Central Cee's 'Sprinter'. And on the flip side, there are songs that have reached No. 1 on both the U.K. and U.S. charts for 10 weeks or more. Think Whitney Houston's 'I Will Always Love You', Ed Sheeran's 'Shape of You', and Harry Styles' 'As It Was'.
[Short music transition]
Host: "It's fascinating to see how music fans in the U.K. and U.S. can have different tastes. 'Rein Me In' is a great example of this. Despite its huge success in the U.K., it's struggling to break through in the U.S. - perhaps due to other popular songs like Olivia Dean's 'Man I Need' and 'So Easy (to Fall in Love)' dominating the charts.
[Closing music starts playing]
Host: "That's all for today, folks. Thanks for tuning in to this update on the world of music charts. We'll be back with more interesting facts and insights soon." [Music fades out]
